chapters.html:
Sixty seconds. That’s how long it took for the world to end.

 

Mydei checked his watch again. Then, he looked around the restaurant they were in, trying to catch a glimpse of familiar pink or golden hair somewhere in the space. To no avail.

Phainon’s frown got a little bit deeper every time Mydei did either of those things. He too wondered where the rest of their friends were, but why did Mydei have to be so obvious about it? It was annoying.

The two of them had been sitting at the bar waiting for the girls for a good forty minutes. Phainon had texted each of them separately asking where they were, to no response.

Phainon checked his own phone again.

 Finally, the screen lit up with a message.

There was a single message from Castorice:

 

Castorice (15:21) 😉

 

Phainon blinked at his phone screen once. Twice. Three times. He felt himself beginning to turn pink, very conscious of the handsome blond man sitting right next to him, the one his friends insisted that he was crushing on hard. Not that Phainon believed them. Him? Have a crush on Mydei? Just the idea was absurd!

But now here he was, sitting at the bar. Just him, a drink, and Mydei, who wore his hair in a cute high ponytail which left his bare neck on full display, and who was dressed in a tight jacket that accentuated his chest, and tighter jeans which clung to every curve of his-

So this was the game they were playing.

Phainon typed his reply with intense rage.

 

Phainon (15:22) I hate you all

 

“Have you heard from them?”

Phainon’s shoulders rose. Mydei was looking at him with intensity, his head slightly cocked so that his strawberry blond fringe dusted against his light eyelashes, his fingers casually curled around his drink, the low light of the bar framing every angle and curve of his face like a painting.

The heat in Phainon’s face flared up with ever greater intensity. He tried not to look, but how could he not look!? How could a man look so good!?

And Phainon was stuck with him. Alone. In a bar. With only his squirming heartbeat and raging horniness for company.

Yep. Phainon was screwed.

“N-no,” he lied in response, trying to cover his face with his phone screen. “Just messaging them again.”

Mydei eyed him for a couple more seconds, before turning back towards the direction of the bar.

“I hope they’re okay,” Mydei said quietly.

“They are!” Phainon replied far too hastily, drawing Mydei’s intense gaze immediately back to himself. Phainon stuttered over an answer. “I-I mean, I’m sure they are!”

Phainon found himself in a greater dilemma. Did he lie to Mydei and say the girls could no longer make it and go home? Did he lie to Mydei and say the girls were severely delayed, but hope Mydei would still stay with him on this set up date that neither would acknowledge as a date?

Or, did he tell Mydei the truth, that their friends had set them up on a date because they believed that Phainon had a ‘crush’ on him that he refused to acknowledge?

Crush? Pfft. Phainon did not have a crush, especially not on Mydei of all people.

The longer Mydei’s gaze remained on him, those rich gold eyes making Phainon’s heart do strange things, the more Phainon really couldn’t make a decision.

Phainon pretended to type on his phone a bit more. “Oh look, that’s Castorice now! She says…they decided to have a girls night instead…She says we should have a fun boys night.” Phainon smiled through the words, even as his eye twitched. He hoped that sounded convincing.

“Boys night?” Mydei questioned with a frown. “Does that mean Anaxa is coming? I thought he had a lecture today?”

“Wow, I didn’t know I was such bad company,” Phainon joked, feigning hurt. Or, pretending to feign. He wasn’t really sure anymore. As awkward as this was, he really didn’t want Mydei to leave.

Mydei was frowning down at his glass, tilting it back and forth so the liquid inside sloshed about unappetisingly. It was an alcoholic drink, though Phainon was pretty sure that Mydei hadn’t had any of it.

“It doesn’t make any sense,” Mydei frowned. “Why would they suddenly change their mind like that and not tell us?”

Next to him, Phainon was trying very hard to not squirm in his seat.

“You know what the girls are like,” Phainon slurred, waving a hand dismissively. He was hoping for a subject change right about now.

Phainon coughed slightly, before leaning over in his seat. He tentatively slipped an arm around Mydei’s shoulders. Something he realised he did quite often, but right now, felt incredibly conscious of. Especially the way that Mydei slightly tilted his head to stare at him from beneath those long lashes of his.

“Besides, we can still have a good time on our own,” Phainon patted Mydei’s shoulders, chuckling nervously. “Right, Mydei? My best buddy?”

Mydei seemed to pout, a little huff falling from his lips, which of course did nothing to Phainon’s absolutely, definitely not, wildly beating heart.

They remained in an awkward silence for quite a few seconds after that. Phainon realised he still had an arm wrapped around Mydei’s shoulders, and should probably retreat.

“So…” Mydei started, his voice cracking slightly. “What do we do?”

Mydei suddenly looked quite awkward sitting on his barstool, a hand going through his hair. Phainon was pretty sure he hadn’t seen Mydei act like this before.

“Well, we, umm…” Phainon looked down at his glass, picking it up. “We talk and drink.”

Mydei looked at the glass, back to Phainon. “Talk and…drink?”

Phainon’s eye twitched again. Why was Mydei being so difficult!?

“Or drink and talk, if you’d prefer that,” Phainon chuckled awkwardly.

“Hmpf,” Mydei pouted, crossing his arms.

Phainon felt the bricks of his own wall going up,his insecurities rising.

“Why are you acting so grumpy?” He asked with more of a bite. “Is it really so hard to talk and drink like a normal person?”

“I can drink and talk just fine,” Mydei responded more defensively, rising to Phainon’s bite.

“Then what’s the problem?” Phainon scowled. “Is it me?”

“I never said that,” Mydei responded.

“Well, you’re sure acting like it is!”

 

And then, just like that, without forewarning, even any kind of hint, those sixty seconds began.

 

Out of nowhere, there was a loud rumble and the ground shuddered. Glass after glass dropped from the shelves behind the bar. Confused mumbles erupted from those around them as the lights flickered overhead, and the ground began to tremble.

Mydei immediately stood from his barstool. He was almost thrown off his feet, and braced himself by holding onto the bar ahead.

“What the heck?” Phainon breathed, trying to make sense of what was happening.

Then, the ground jolted much more harshly beneath their feet.

Phainon found himself flung from his barstool. His glass soon followed him, splaying broken glass at his face. He managed to shield his face with his hands. He winced as he felt some of the glass cut his neck, his hands.

Several loud booms rang out from somewhere overhead, and Phainon covered his ears. The ground seemed to slant and groan out. Furniture toppled all around him. His ears rang, the world seemed to spin.

“Phainon!”

When Phainon looked up again, it was to Mydei grabbing his hand and pulling him up. Phainon’s hands were red with blood, staining Mydei’s own as he gripped onto him tightly.

For the first time, Phainon saw panic in Mydei’s golden eyes.

Ahead of them, everyone else in the bar was heading for the door, screaming as they tried to leave.

The two of them didn’t say a word and quickly followed.

As they headed towards the doors, Phainon could see the light drain from the outside world. The sun was dimming. Replacing it, an eerie red glow.

By the time they burst outside, the blue sky was gone. Instead, it was washed inky blacks and reds. A red glow seemed to rise from the city skyscrapers beyond, casting dark shadows on everything below. Most glass windows had shattered. A heavy wind had picked up, blowing papers, glass and ash along the streets. Clothes and belongings had been abandoned on the sidewalk. Dogs were barking, children were screaming. People were trying to run, but seemingly had no idea where to go. What was happening.

As Phainon and Mydei gazed up at the red sky, two cars collided with each other right ahead of them in the street. Phainon felt the heat from the explosion on his skin, felt the force of it try to push him off his feet. Everything was overwhelming Phainon’s senses.

“Mydei, what’s happening?!” Phainon cried out, hoping the other would have an answer.

Mydei said nothing. He could only stare in shock, his hand still tightly clutched around Phainon’s own.

That was when the shadows seemed to get darker, and the screaming got louder. A woman besides them fell to her knees, pulling at her hair as she screamed.

The next moment, she was consumed by black and red flames.

The two of them stumbled backwards. The heat was blazing and intense, the cries enough to bring Phainon to his knees. It was only Mydei’s grip that kept him upright.

Phainon watched the people around them burst into red flames. One by one. As if the air was so hot that their bodies simply set aflame on the spot. The cries were lucid in his ears, sounds of desperate dying pleads, curdling into grotesque screams, sounds he would surely never forget. All down the street, as far as he could see, people went up in red flames.

Then, their bodies seemed to morph. Phainon heard cracking sounds ringing through his ears, as if bodies were turning to stone.

Once the flames dissipated, there was no trace of any person.

The woman who had once been standing besides them stopped screaming. The flames died. An alien creature stood in her place. No eyes. Blades carved out of her arms. Her entire body was hunched grotesquely, and made entirely of stone.

All the people who had once been around them were turning into the exact same monsters.

Phainon couldn’t move, couldn’t think. His hand slipped from Mydei’s, his eyes glued to the scene ahead. Tears that he couldn’t feel streamed from his eyes. It should have been a nightmare, but the blood dripping from his hands, the undying screams in his ears, told him it was all real.

Everything around him was dying, burning, and there was nothing he could do. No way he could help. No way he could even process what was happening.

The monster nearest to them craned its neck, its eyeless head glaring straight at the two of them. An unintelligible carnal roar came from it, and then it charged for them. 

“Phainon!”

Mydei grabbed his hand again, and dragged them into a run.

Mydei’s grip was so tight, as if whatever else happened, he would never let go.

That was enough to pull Phainon back, to focus.

He saw Mydei ahead of him, screaming at him to snap out of it. To run faster. Mydei’s hair was a mess, his eyes wide with panic. Blood stains were smeared across his cheek, his hands. His clothes were shredded.

The world around them was falling apart.

But, Mydei was still here.

When a monster slammed around the nearest bend, aiming straight for Mydei’s head, Phainon was quick to react.

“Mydei!”

Phainon pushed Mydei to the floor. The bladed arm of the monster slashed through the air where Mydei had been just a moment prior. A ruined car door lay on the floor beside them. Phainon picked it up, yelling as he swung it at the monster’s face. It was enough to make the monster stumble backwards. It gave Mydei enough time to get back onto his feet. This time, Phainon took his hand and dragged them forwards.

“Where do we go!?” Phainon cried as they ran, breathless and with no sense of direction. “W-what do we do!?”

“I know a place!” Mydei shouted back, his golden eyes almost luminous in the now darkened world. “It’s not too far. Grab as many supplies on the way as you can! And stay close!”

 

Mydei led them to an abandoned office building. Around the far side was a trapdoor, which they were heading straight towards. 

The scenes they’d passed on the way were unlike anything Phainon could ever describe.

They’d looted a small shop for some tinned food, grabbing what they could and stuffing it in their pockets. Mydei had even found a rifle which he had now strapped over his chest.

However, they had attracted a group of monsters that was currently pursuing them at pace.

Mydei fumbled in his pocket, pulling out an old looking key. Phainon watched his hands shake as he tried to insert the key into the lock on the trapdoor whilst the monster’s roars drew closer. Above them, the sky thundered, growing ever darker over their heads.

“Get in!” Mydei yelled as soon as he’d pried the door open. He shoved Phainon in first, before following closely behind, slamming the trapdoor shut on the approaching monster’s face. The thing wrestled to try and pull the door open again. Mydei yelled out, struggling against it. Phainon came behind him on the ladder, grabbing the handle also.

“Pull!”

With their combined strength, they managed to pull the trapdoor down. The sounds of the outside world were immediately muted. The awful red colour of the sky was shut out, replaced with complete darkness. Mydei quickly locked the trapdoor in place afterward. The monsters continued to scream and hammer at the door overhead.

For a few moments, all Phainon could take in was the sound of his own heartbeat, and Mydei’s harsh breathing beside his own. They were in the dark now. Everything slowly began catching up to him, and he found himself crashing onto the floor, holding his head as he tried to process it, trying to convince himself that the sounds and sights of the outside world weren’t real.

But they were.

Mydei joined him on the floor quickly after. The two of them sat panting in the darkness, flinching whenever the monster banged violently on the trapdoor above their heads.

They continued to sit close together in the dark until the banging sounds from the monster overhead finally died. It seemed the thing chasing them had finally lost interest.

But beyond that, Phainon could hear the sounds of the raging wind, thunder, explosions across the city, and worst of all, so much screaming.

He felt Mydei shuffle next to him. Then, the small click of a light switch.

A singular light turned on above their heads, revealing the place that Mydei had brought them to. It looked like a small bunker. A pile of blankets on the floor for a bed. A small desk, a shelf of books and candles, a small stove with some basic kitchen utensils, and an old tub. There was an old radio on the desk, alongside a first aid kit. Cans of tinned and dry food lined one of the shelves of the bookcase, and there was a tap in the corner, implying this place had working water.

Mydei seemed to take a deep breath, before dusting his hands across the desk, looking at the dust collecting on his fingertips. He didn’t say anything.

Phainon watched Mydei, whose clothes were now ruined, who had blood on his hands, in his hair. Mydei’s hands were still trembling, and his usually unwavering eyes seemed shaken to the core. He must’ve been able to hear the grotesque noises from above their heads too.

Now he was sitting still in the dark, Phainon found his tears coming back. He began to cry quietly, clutching his head.

“What’s happening…?” Phainon mumbled. “How is this possible…?”

He found himself shakily reaching into his pocket and pulling out his phone, uncaring that his hands were still bleeding and he was getting blood all over his phone screen. His phone had a large crack going down the middle of the screen. When he tried to swipe the touchscreen, it didn’t do anything. What was worse, the top right read that there was no signal.

Phainon choked a sob as he looked at his phone screen. A picture of him with all his friends. Aglaea. Castorice. Anaxa. Hyacine. Cipher. Cyrene. And Mydei. He was in the middle of the picture, an arm around them all. They were all smiling.

“The-the others…How am I supposed to know if…” Tears streaked down his face. “What if they’re like…all those people…” He gripped his hair tightly. “All those people…I couldn’t save anyone…do anything…” He curled into himself. “What the hell? Why is this happening?!”

Mydei still didn't say anything. Perhaps he simply didn’t know what to say. Perhaps there was nothing he could say that would make the situation better.

“There’s no signal down here,” Mydei said after a long while. He had his back turned to Phainon, his fists clenching hard. “We just have to hope they are like us, and found somewhere safe to shelter.”

A boom sounded over their heads.

“I hope so…” Phainon slurred, “I hope so.”

His friends were strong, he knew that. But they’d run through the entire city to get here, and they’d not seen any other person at all. Only monsters, and those becoming them.

There was every chance that all their friends had also become….

“You’re hurt,” Mydei said.

Phainon’s eyes focused again. He saw Mydei coming toward him carrying a first aid kit.

Phainon watched Mydei kneel in front of him and open the first aid kit. He let Mydei take his hands. Phainon zoned in and out as Mydei cleaned his bloodied hands with a damp towel and antibiotic ointment. He watched Mydei delicately tie bandages around his palms. A couple of Phainon’s tears fell between them in the silence.

“All those people…” Phainon started after a while. “…Why were we the only ones who were spared?”

Mydei didn’t look at him, continuing to focus on wrapping the bandages.

“…We should be careful with how much we use this kit,” He responded after a while. “It’s the only one down here.” Mydei tied the bandages in place. “Try these for now. If you bleed through, I’ll change them.”

Phainon finally found himself focusing on Mydei again. Mydei who was holding his hands as he secured the bandages, his own strong hands shaking, but his touch still sensitive and soft as always.

The fact that Mydei was here with him might’ve been the only grounding thing he had, the only bit of relief from the chaos overhead.

“Mydei,” Phainon said, “Where are we?”

Mydei sighed gently. “This is a bunker built by my mother and father. They built it…in case something like this were to happen.” Mydei looked down at the floor. “Little did they know we were going to live till the day to see it.”

Phainon blinked at him. “Do you know something about what’s happening?”

Mydei closed his eyes, as if that might stop the way he continued to tremble. He let out an exhale. “My father was a paranoid man. He was obsessed with this supposed phenomena which turned people into monsters of stone. He called it the black tide.”

“The black tide…”

“I always thought he was just insane,” Mydei sighed.  “But, my mother never seemed to doubt him… and now, he might be the only reason we’re still alive.”

Another boom overhead and the whole bunker seemed to shake. Dust fell from the ceiling.

“Mydei!”

Phainon rushed forward, hugging himself around the other man as if to shield him from any incoming attack. Nothing ever came.

Even when the shuddering stopped, Phainon didn’t let go. His tears stained Mydei’s shoulders.

“I don’t know what I would’ve done if you’d become a monster…” Phainon whispered, clutching to him.

Mydei didn’t say anything. Instead, he tentatively wound his own arms around Phainon. Their bodies lay flush in an embrace. Phainon could  feel the way Mydei’s body trembled, could even feel the fast beating of the other’s heart through their chests.

“As long as you’re here…” Phainon whimpered, “Promise me that you’ll stay here with me, Mydei.” Phainon buried his head against the crook of Mydei’s neck. “Until the end, stay here with me.”

He heard Mydei suck in a breath. “I promise…” He whispered.

Phainon hugged him tightly. He tried to soothe himself in Mydei’s scent. Damp and rusty, with a slight hint of cinnamon.

Right now, you’re the only thing I have.

And there is no chance I’m letting you go.

Phainon wasn’t sure how long they simply hugged in silence, sharing that vulnerable, uncertain moment. It wasn’t really silence, not when they could still hear the chaos locked outside.

Right at that moment, Phainon only allowed himself to focus on the feel of Mydei’s raging heartbeat through their chests.

 

Later, they went through the supplies they had. Mydei estimated they had enough food to last for over a month, maybe even 2 months if they were resourceful. They still had running water, but again, they’d be conservative. The water was attached to a tanker that would run out eventually, and with what was happening outside, drinking rain water might not be safe.

With the constant rumbling over their heads, there was no way to tell exactly what was happening outside, nor how long they would have to hide in the bunker. But, they would remain in place. They would wait out for a sign that it was safe outside. They would ration supplies, and keep noise to a minimum as to not attract anymore monsters to their location.

Amongst the supplies, Phainon found an old diary. Upon flicking it open, he found only the first page was written on. The writing was curved and elegant, and perfectly neat. Phainon began to read the words written on the page:

 

To my dear son, Mydeimos. Me and your father have built this place from our own hands for you. I hope that with this hideout, that we can protect you, even when we are no longer here by your side in person. Should the worst ever come to pass, and you no longer know what to do, come here.

By the time this place comes of use to you, we will likely no longer be here. But we will never be gone completely. I hope you can feel the love we hold for you resonating from these four walls.

Keep yourself safe, my dear beloved son.

We love you so much,

Mum and Dad x             

 

Phainon almost felt guilty, reading those words. It didn’t stop him clutching the notebook to his chest and closing his eyes, imagining that he too could feel the warm embrace promised by those comforting words.

Phainon was currently sitting on the pile of blankets that would be their bed. Mydei was by the desk. He’d been tinkering with the radio; it seemed it was broken. Or perhaps fiddling with the parts was enough to distract his mind from the ceaseless noises outside.

With screaming, and explosions still ringing overhead, Phainon picked up the diary and a pen, and began to write.

 

Day 1. The world has ended.

We had no time to do anything. Black and red washed out the sky. People all around us turned into monsters. Mydei grabbed my hand and we just ran. Somehow, we managed to get to this place.

We’re not sure why everyone else turned to monsters except us. We don’t even know if our friends are okay. We can still hear screaming and thunder from the surface, alongside many other awful sounds. Both of us can’t bear to listen to it. I know Mydei, he’s desperate to go out there and try to help, as am I. But we’ve managed to hold each other back. It’s just the two of us now, and I’m not losing him.

There is water and blankets here, and enough food to last us a couple months if we have to. I hope it won’t be that long, but we will do whatever it takes to survive this. Me and Mydei have promised that we are in this together, until the end. 

Miss Gorgo, you and your son are the only reason why I’m still alive. He pulled me up when I couldn’t walk forward. And this place that you and your husband built is keeping us alive right now.

Your son has grown into an incredible young man. I promise you that I’ll devote the rest of my life to keeping him safe. Whilst he’s with me, nothing ill will happen to him, not ever.

Signed, Phainon.

 

Hours later, Phainon checked his phone again. It was night, and yet the noises above them hadn’t ceased. He felt a squirming sensation all over his body the longer those awful noises resonated through his head.

Mydei had given up trying to fix the radio for now.

“It’s late,” Mydei said quietly. “We should try to sleep.”

Phainon nodded in response. He looked to the pile of blankets that would be their bed. Had this not been the end of the world, Phainon may have had palpitations at the thought of sharing a bed with Mydei, especially when Mydei lifted his shirt over his head, and hung it over the back of a chair.

Even now, despite everything, Phainon still felt his throat seize up slightly at the sight of Mydei’s toned chest.

He swallowed it down, removing his own shirt. It was a little difficult with his bandaged hands.

Phainon was already sitting on the blankets, and simply slipped himself under and lowered himself onto a pillow. Mydei joined him afterward, shuffling under the same blanket and laying down.

Phainon was conscious that Mydei still kept a respectful distance between their bodies, making sure he was at the edge of the blanket. Phainon could just about sense his body heat, enough to bring just the slightest bit of warmth.

“Goodnight…” Phainon whispered quietly. Mydei didn’t reply straight away, and Phainon wondered if the other man hadn’t heard him over the constant droning above their heads.

“Goodnight,” came an eventual quiet reply.

After that, nothing else was said. Phainon couldn’t even hear himself breathing. The sounds above them continued to wail out. Phainon felt tears prick his eyes. He kept flinching at every loud boom in the distance, every sudden scream. To listen to it, and imagine what was happening out there, where his friends were, it was torture.

After a while, Phainon found himself turning his head in Mydei’s direction. Mydei faced away from Phainon, his hair splayed across the pillow, the blanket pulled right up to his chin. From how the fabric dipped, he seemed to be clutching part of the blanket in his fist.

Or was he…hugging his arms around himself?

Phainon had no doubts that Mydei was awake as well. How could he ever sleep peacefully like this?

Phainon found himself turning over, so he could face Mydei fully. Tentatively, he reached out a hand, until he was just barely brushing Mydei’s back.

Mydei flinched slightly at the touch. After a while, Phainon felt him lean back slightly, until Phainon’s hand could press flat against the top of his back.

Phainon let out a breathy exhale. That simple touch gave him so much relief. Now that he could feel Mydei’s weight, he found his eyes could finally close.

No matter what, it was going to be a long night, and neither knew what was ahead.

As long as I have him, Phainon mouthed to himself.

As long as I have him.

 

…

 

That was how the days began to pass.

 

Day 2: The noise outside is still so loud, and it feels like it’s getting colder in here. The battery on my phone is running out. I turned it off for now to try and preserve it. Me and Mydei are still trying to fix the radio, but it’s in a worse state than we thought.

The noises I can hear make me feel sick, and yet I still can’t help but feel hungry, is that selfish of me?

I’m scared, and I know Mydei is too even if he won’t admit to it…I wish I could comfort him better.

 

Day 3: The noises outside are getting quieter. I can’t hear screaming anymore. What I can hear is unlike anything I can describe. Mydei’s guess is that it’s the abominations wandering about, feasting on whatever remains up there.

My hands are getting better, Mydei says. Luckily I managed to avoid getting an infection. It’s all thanks to him. I don’t know what I’d do if he wasn’t here with me.

 

It felt much colder in the bunker by the third night, so much that Phainon could see the fog from his own breath. Phainon didn’t think the temperature drop was just constrained to their small bunker. Outside, he imagined the temperature had dropped far more drastically.

Phainon was still shivering under the blankets as he tried to sleep. Lying beside him, Mydei was doing the same thing. Mydei had raised his shoulders high, and had wrapped his arms around his own torso. Phainon lay facing him, tracing his form with his eyes as if that could distract him from the cold.

What accompanied them from above sounded like rainfall, still not enough to sedate either into sleep.

Phainon knew neither of them were going to be able to sleep unless they found a way to get warmer.

Phainon opened and closed his mouth several times, trying to figure out how to approach this. He and Mydei had known each other for a good couple of years, introduced to each other by their shared friends. Phainon had always had a soft spot for him, no matter how much they used to bicker, and how awkward Mydei could be sometimes.

“…Phainon?” Came a low voice, pulling Phainon from his thoughts.

“Yes?” Phaion asked, looking at the back of Mydei’s head.

“…Are you cold?”

Phainon bit his lip. It even tasted cold. “…A little. What about you?”

Mydei didn’t respond straight away. Phainon watched his shoulders rise and fall a couple times, watched the minute movements in his back.

“We shouldn’t let ourselves get sick from the cold,” Mydei said. “We should share body heat.”

Phainon swallowed once. “…Okay.”

Mydei sighed gently, before turning over. Phainon stayed still, letting Mydei approach him. They shuffled closer together, until Phainon found himself resting against the side of Mydei’s neck. His arms were around Mydei’s torso. One of Mydei’s arms nervously rested against his back. Immediately, Phainon felt the heat radiating from the other’s body. He could feel it stirring something warm inside himself.

The embrace was stiff, and it remained that way even after Phainon guessed that several minutes had passed.

Even at the end of the world, it seemed that intimacy remained awkward for Mydei.

But with their bodies now being so close, Phainon could feel the way Mydei’s body flinched and seized at the slightest of unknown sounds above their heads.

Phainon didn’t dare move. That desire to try and comfort Mydei rose high in his chest again. However, he still couldn’t work out how to cross that boundary between them.

Phainon waited and waited, until he felt Mydei’s breathing lull and even out, and his shoulders finally relaxed into sleep. When he was sure that Mydei was asleep, Phainon buried his head against the crook Mydei’s neck. He took a deep breath. Despite the fact that Mydei had yet to shower, his scent remained much the same as usual, to Phainon’s relief. Beneath the sweat and grime, the delicate trace of cinnamon that Phainon loved so much.

In an embrace with Mydei, lulled by his scent, the cold had dissipated, and the outside world felt much further away than before. Enough that Phainon could finally fall asleep.

After that, they cuddled beneath the blankets - exchanging body heat as Mydei called it - every night.

 

Day 5: It’s completely silent above our heads now. I can’t even hear any rain like before. But that silence is deafening.

Both our phones are completely dead now. Any hope of contacting someone from outside is gone, unless we can get that radio fixed.

Mydei offered to go outside and check our surroundings, but I held him back. Anything could be up there. We are safe down here and have bountiful supplies. I’m not going to let him risk his own life like that.

Besides, the two of us can find plenty of ways to pass the time. There’s pens and paper down here, so I suggested that he should try drawing something. He turned his nose up at that for now. His pouty face is quite adorable, that hasn’t changed.

 

Mydei continued to try and fix the radio again the next day. Phainon could see that whenever Mydei was working on fixing the radio, that his mind was elsewhere. As was Phainon’s. A lot had happened. A lot remained a mystery.

It had been seven days since they’d locked themselves inside the bunker. The world outside had been deathly quiet for three days. Neither of them knew if the outside world still existed at all.

Phainon had been sitting on the desk beside Mydei, watching him tinker with the radio frequency, when the thing suddenly squealed.

Both of them jumped back as a monotone woman’s voice came from the radio speakers.

“This is an emergency message. Any survivors, seek shelter immediately. Find the safest place. Remain there until further notice. Do not go outside under any circumstance.”

After that, they could hear the thundering and screaming sounds that they had both heard when the black tide first came. A different woman’s voice started speaking, this one startled and breathless as if she were running.

“They’ve called it the Black Tide. It came from nowhere without warning. It took the light. It split the ground. It turned many into mindless creatures. Then it started raining red blood. All I can see are monsters. They don’t have eyes but still they pursue me. If anyone is still out there, please, don’t come out here! Don’t come out!”

Before the broadcaster could say anymore, she was suddenly cut off with a scream.

Then, the radio went back to static.

Phainon felt sick to his stomach.

Mydei didn’t say anything for a long time after the radio returned to silence. Phainon could see his brow twitching, the way he struggled to keep his restless hands still. Perhaps he was thinking about their friends, everything they’d left behind, everything that had been ravaged and destroyed whilst they sat down here.

It was true. The world really had ended. There really was a chance that there was nothing left of their friends, their old lives. It made Phainon want to scream and scream until his lungs couldn’t take it any longer.

There was only one thing that stopped him from giving in.

Phainon approached him slowly.

He reached out, gently taking Mydei’s hand.

Mydei’s breath hitched slightly, and he looked over his shoulder, down at the hand encasing his own.

When his eyes wound their way up to look at Phainon’s eyes, Phainon responded by squeezing his hand, and sending him a smile.

Mydei stared at him for several seconds, before looking back down at the floor. He didn’t pull away.

They stayed like that, holding hands in the static.

Phainon hoped that with that smile, he could provide Mydei with just a little bit of relief amongst this stagnant chaos.

Though really, that smile could have meant anything.

 

Day 9: Our food rations are good and our water supplies stable. My hands are completely healed now.

I took a bath today. To conserve water we are sharing bath water. I offered for Mydei to bathe first but he insisted it be me first. He went off to the other side of the bunker to give me some privacy whilst I bathed. It’s kind of a shame. I would have quite liked to have bathed in Mydei’s bath water. Maybe another time. We have a lot of time down here, after all.

We did have to share a towel, however.

That’s fine. The towel smells like Mydei.

I feel like since we got trapped down here, I’ve become obsessed with his scent even more than I used to be.

But, the world ended, how could I still have feelings for him?

 

Day 12: Mydei spends most of the time perched next to the radio, waiting for the next incoming transmission that will hopefully set us free. Every now and then the same emergency broadcast plays. Other than that, nothing.

It makes me sad to see that grave expression on Mydei’s face. So, I gave him the drawing supplies again and suggested he draw something. Anything. I told him that he could even draw me in nude if he wanted.

He refused at first, but whilst I tried to nap, I noticed him picking up the pencils and paper. He’s been drawing quietly ever since. He won’t even let me peek at his creation. His eyes keep flitting my way. Is he actually drawing me nude?

 

Phainon’s sleep became plagued by nightmares. Every time he tried to sleep, he saw flashbacks to that day. The glasses falling from the bar, the sky going red, bones cracking and screams flaring as the people around him turned into brainless stone monsters.

In his dream, he saw the monster that had pursued them as they tried to flee with their lives. He watched it play out again and again; the monster lunged at Mydei, a bladed hand aimed right at his neck. Phainon screamed Mydei’s name, trying to reach out to save him.

Only this time, he wasn’t going to get there in time.

“Mydei!”

The next moment, Phainon jolted awake. He was sweating all over, his hands tightly clamped around the blankets that made up his bed. Before him stretched the quiet bunker that he and Mydei had been living in for almost two weeks.

Phainon wiped his hands over his face, trying to wash out thoughts of those nightmares, trying to ground himself in the way his hands trembled, in the rhythmic beat of his own heart.

 He felt someone else stir beside him.

“Are you alright?” Mydei asked, his voice barely a whisper, as if he already knew the answer to that.

Mydei was still lying down against the sheets. He had an arm resting above his head, and his hair splayed out messily against the pillows, but his eyes were raw with concern.

“Sorry, did I wake you up?” Phainon tried to smile at him. “I’m alright, just a nightmare, please, go back to sleep.”

Mydei observed him for a moment. He seemed to bite his lip. “…Are you not going to sleep?” He asked quietly.

“I will. Just…give me a minute.”

Phainon fiddled with the edges of the blankets as he waited for Mydei to stop looking at him and drift back off to sleep.

It shouldn’t have been a big deal. Having nightmares after everything they witnessed together only made sense. And yet, Phainon couldn’t help but feel embarrassed. He wanted to put on a brave face for Mydei. He wanted to heed Gorgo’s words in the diary, and protect her son on her behalf. He didn’t want the other to see this side of himself.

Eventually, Phainon felt brave enough to peek back at Mydei again. Mydei had his eyes closed, his breath lulled.

Phainon couldn’t help but think about how pretty Mydei looked whilst he was asleep. Tussled strawberry blond hair. Long sweeping eyelashes. Defined collar bones. The sight of Mydei like that helped to calm Phainon’s racing heartbeat somewhat. And the thought of Mydei’s reaction to finding that Phainon thought him pretty was quite amusing to imagine.

Mydei had an arm slightly outstretched on the pillow, a gap perfectly made for a certain white-haired man who slept beside him.

Phainon finally sighed, a little smile on his lips, and nestled back down against Mydei’s arm. He concentrated on the feeling of Mydei’s arm pressing against his side, and closed his eyes.

Some time passed. Phainon had still yet to find sleep. He wasn’t sure if he would tonight.

Especially not when he heard Mydei breathe heavily, before wrapping his arms around Phainon’s chest, and pulling their backs flush.

Phainon was so shocked that he probably held his breath for a couple minutes. Mydei’s chest was firmly pressed against his back. His two strong arms woven around Phainon’s front. Phainon could feel the tip of his nose lightly touching the back of his neck, and he could feel Mydei’s hair against his shoulder.

Phainon raised his hands to his face, feeling how hot he’d become. He couldn’t stop himself blushing.

If this was Mydei’s special way of dissipating the night terrors, then it was working.

Even still, Phainon had to pout a little. He wanted to be the big spoon.

 

Day 14: Two weeks have passed. I can feel my sanity slipping. Perhaps it would have gone already had Mydei not been here with me.

We’ve done a lot of talking. There isn’t much else to do. But I quite like listening to Mydei talk. He’s never been much of a talker, perhaps he still finds it awkward to do small talk like this. But I’ve started to notice tell-tale signs on him. When we talk about art and cooking his eyes light up. When I try to tease him he doesn’t always get the joke, but when he does, he tilts his head away and bites his lip. He really is so cute when he does that. Every now and then, I’m sure I can see pink on his cheeks, but maybe that’s just my imagination.

Perhaps it’s a bad idea to try and make jokes these days. But that’s how me and Mydei have always been. Maybe I’m just trying to give a little sense of normalcy amongst all this.

 

A few nights later, Phainon was woken by a soft groaning next to his ear.

He looked over to Mydei, only to find his face scrunched up deeply in his sleep. Sweat rolled down the sides of his face from his forehead. He was mumbling nothings, his head tossing from side to side.

Phainon’s heart broke at the sight. He’d been wishing for Mydei to let his guard down more around him, but he didn’t want to see him struggling like this.

For how long had Mydei been having night terrors like this? How well had he been hiding them?

Mydei had been cuddling Phainon for the past few nights.

Whilst Mydei continued to groan, Phainon flipped himself around, making sure to embrace him tightly instead. He pulled Mydei’s chest against his own, a hand around his waist. He quietly directed Mydei’s head to lie against the crook of his neck.

Mydei whimpered once, then went still. His expression softened, his nightmare dissipating. A gentler sleep overcame him.

Phainon observed him for a while, a deep sense of fondness settling in his chest. He felt the urge to reach out and brush his fingers through Mydei’s hair, and ended up doing so very gently. Despite the little food they ate, and how they limited their baths to every five days, Mydei’s hair was so soft. His hair had noticeably grown since coming to the bunker. Where the tips of his hair once dusted his shoulders, it now continued extending, curling naturally at the ends. Phainon thought the natural curls were adorable. His fringe was longer also. Phainon should probably offer to trim it for him, or would the tips of his fringe start curling eventually too?

Mydei was clearly asleep. Phainon decided that he would indulge his urge just once.

Very carefully, he craned his neck slightly, so he could place a chaste kiss to the top of Mydei’s forehead.

 

Day 17: Mydei won’t admit to his nightmares, but I’ll make sure that he’s always held tightly from now on. That’s the least I can do for him.

He looked quite startled when we got into bed and I immediately pulled him taunt against my chest. He asked what I was doing. When I said I was spooning him he went completely silent. He said nothing else for the rest of the night.

Has he never been little spoon before?

I lay awake watching him, making sure his night terrors stayed away. From his expression, they flared up a couple times. I found out that squeezing him a little tighter and whispering reassurance was enough to make them go away again. At least for now.

It satiates something in my own mind that I can care for him like this. It makes me much happier than it should. I guess I can’t deny that crush on him anymore.

He really is the only thing keeping me sane.

 

Day 20: We still have a good amount of food and water. I’m starting to get used to the feeling of hunger and of feeling dirty. There is still no news from the radio. We heard a few gunshots throughout the day, but it gives little hints as to what’s happening up there.

A week ago I might have wondered how I would ever get used to life down here. One would think that staying in a small confined space at the end of the world would be torture. I think it would be, were I not here with Mydei.

Ever since I started spooning him in bed, he’s begun to open up a little bit more. Sometimes he almost feels like a new man to me. I never knew that he liked history so much, he’s a complete whizz on Ancient Greek and Roman histories. Hearing him talk about it with so much passion makes my heart beat. And when I talk to him about antiques, he always listens so intently, even lets a smile slip from time to time.

We talked about our dreams in life too. I never knew that Mydei wanted to find love. I feel somewhat jealous. But he says there is no point to it anymore. Or at least, not until we can leave this bunker safely.

Some sick part of me hopes it really will just be the two of us from now on, because if it is just the two of us then surely he will fall for me eventually.

Perhaps the end of the world reveals people’s true colours.

What must he think of mine?

 

A few days later, they both filled up the old tub they used for bathing. It was difficult to heat the water with just a small stove to provide heat, but they managed to get the temperature to about lukewarm.

Once it was ready, Phainon signalled to Mydei.

“You go first,” he said. “I went first last time, so it’s your turn.”

Rather than agreeing – or even disagreeing – Mydei bit his lip instead.

“We could just bathe together,” he said quietly.

Phainon blinked once. Twice.

He looked to the bathtub. Or, the old barrel that had become one. It was tight with only one person in there, let alone the two of them.

“P-pardon?”

“It will help conserve water and save soap if we just bathe together.” Mydei scratched the side of his head. He blushed slightly. “I don’t mind…unless you have a problem with it?”

Phainon flailed his arms about. “Nope. No problems here! Makes no difference to me!”

Phainon watched Mydei throw off his top. As Mydei took off his jeans and his boxers, Phainon couldn’t help but gawk. It wasn’t like they hadn’t seen each other undress before. They’d been living in a tight space together for almost three weeks, it was impossible not to accidentally see glances of each other here and there.

They’d been living in the bunker for almost three weeks by now, and Phainon could now see the effects of living off rationed soup and stress on Mydei’s body. His once perfectly sculpted chest was still impressive. However, Phainon had seen Mydei’s body enough to know his arms weren’t as broad as they used to be, and his chest was less defined now. Phainon could only imagine that his own body was the same.

Part of Phainon felt deeply sorrowful to see Mydei’s perfect body beginning to fade. The other part – that wretched possessive part of himself - squealed at the thought of Mydei lacking the strength he once had, of needing someone to protect him.

But still, no matter what became of their muscles, bathing with Mydei in a tiny tub was a whole different thing to cuddling him in bed.

Phainon let Mydei get settled in the tub first, before stripping himself, and climbing in beside him.

The only way for both of them to fit together was if their bodies were pressed close together. Their shoulders touching, their feet winding between each other. Phainon was so close to Mydei’s face that he could see little freckles across his cheeks, something he’d never even noticed before.

Phainon’s heart beat so incredibly fast. The water was barely warm, and yet he could feel steam rising from the water between them.

He shouldn’t be feeling such things at the end of the world, but Mydei was just so damn attractive.

Mydei washed himself lightly with the soap – apparently he hadn’t noticed the effect he was having on the other in the tub - before handing it to Phainon to use. Phainon washed himself quietly, trying not to look Mydei’s way too obviously.

Once he was done, they sat quietly in the tub for a few moments. Mydei had his eyes closed. His damp hair stuck to his face. Water dripped rhythmically from his chin. He looked quite tranquil like that.

A month ago, there was no way Mydei would have done something like this with him.

Eventually, Phainon cleared his throat to get his attention. Mydei peaked one eye open at him. Phainon held up the bar of soap.

“I’ll wash your back for you,” Phainon said, simulating a twirling motion. “Turn around.”

Mydei blinked his eyes closed, before heeding Phainon’s command without argument. He spun around, until his back faced Phainon.

Phainon rubbed soap over his hands, and began massaging it into Mydei’s back. He pressed his thumbs against Mydei’s shoulder blades, hoping he could help relieve some of the other’s tension. He didn’t miss the way that Mydei shuddered audibly as his palms trailed over a certain spot on his back. Apparently he was extra sensitive there. Phainon could see Mydei’s ears going pink. Was he embarrassed by the noise he’d just made?

Phainon decided he would lock that memory away for later. He would replay that noise in his mind tonight over and over.

“Want me to wash your hair too?” Phainon asked. He twirled a finger through the ends of Mydei’s hair. “It’s getting quite long now. You should try and look after it.”

“Sure,” Mydei replied simply.

Mydei hummed as Phainon tangled his fingers through his hair, brushing out the knots and kinks. Phainon scratched against his scalp, hoping that would make Mydei relax even more.

Mydei began to sink deeper into the water, huffing and humming lightly now and then. By the time Phainon was done, Mydei was resting against his chest.

Phainon peeked at him, brushing some stray hair from his eyes. He was surprised that Mydei still had his eyes closed, a gentle smile on his lips.

The sight was nothing less than breath-taking.

“Did you like that, Mydeimos?” Phainon asked in a hushed tone, caressing fingers through his soft hair.

“Hmm.”                       

Mydei leaned into his touch, and Phainon felt his pulse sky-rocketing.

“Mydei?” Phainon asked quietly, deciding to press forward. He was still brushing his hands through Mydei’s hair. “…Would you kill me if I said you’re cute?”

Mydei was silent. He didn’t even open his eyes.

“…Don’t ruin this moment, Phainon,” he said after a while.

“Is that a yes or a no?”

Mydei groaned. Even so, he was yet to stop Phainon from touching him, and he was yet to peel his back from Phainon’s chest.

“You’re annoying,” was all he mumbled.

Phainon found himself chuckling lightly at that. He was tempted to lean down and kiss Mydei again. He wondered what his reaction would be. He decided he’d hold back and let Mydei rest for now.

 

They had been sleeping peacefully. Phainon had managed to drift off for once. He was hugging Mydei to his chest like he was a giant teddy bear. Mydei was also sound asleep. He had once leg propped up slightly, his hands curled around the edges of his pillow as he slept.

There had been some banging above them for a couple nights in a row, but there was no way to tell if it was human or not.

Only when there was a loud bang and the sound of yelling did the two of them wake.

“What’s going on!?” Phainon exclaimed.

Mydei was already to his feet and grabbing the rifle.

“Grab a dagger, protect yourself!” He screamed.

 

Day 24: Those gunshots we heard the other day turned out to be people.

Bad people.

We were awoken rudely in the night by raiders. We don’t know exactly how they found us, but they were able to break the lock and get inside the bunker. There were about four of them. They’d covered their faces and they were armed, though they seemed hesitant to use their weapons against us. They said they wouldn’t hurt us if we let them take what they wanted. Mydei wouldn’t put up with that, and neither would I. We fought back, but they still managed to take half of our food supplies. We were lucky that neither of us got injured.

Mydei has a spare padlock. We decided to lock the door from the inside. Hopefully no one else can get in, and hopefully the raiders won’t come back. But now they know we are here and have food, it’s unlikely that they’ll leave us be, unless something happens to them first.

Part of me is relieved just to see another person after so long. It’s proof that not everyone is gone, perhaps there is still hope for our friends. But our food supply is now a worry. Mydei told me not to stress over it. If there are other people out there then it may now be safe to check out the surface again.

I told him to hold off for now. We shouldn’t rush into anything. The food we have left will still last another week.

Mydei took the key for the padlock. He won’t tell me where he’s hidden it no matter how much I pester him. Does he not trust me even after all we’ve been through?

 

Day 26: The raiders tried to come back. Luckily this time we fended them off with the rifle before they could break our padlock.

Our food supplies are a real concern. If we don’t go and look for food, we will run out pretty soon. Mydei wants to go up to the surface. I’ve convinced him to wait a little longer.

In truth, I’m absolutely terrified to open that door. What if something happens to him?

 

Day 29: Our food is low. Our water is low. Our morale is low.

Perhaps I’m going insane, the way I cling to him, the way I beg him to stay. Or perhaps I’m just selfish, keeping him to myself.

But I won’t take it back. I promised I’d keep him safe, and I’ll do anything to achieve that, whether he likes it or not.

 

“Mydei, you can’t!”

Phainon grabbed Mydei’s arm, restraining him. Mydei spun back to him. He gritted his teeth, his expression grave.

“We have no food, Phainon. If one of us doesn’t go up and look for supplies, we’ll starve.”

“It’s too soon. We don’t know what it’s like up there!” Phainon argued.

“The same group of people have tried to raid us twice,” Mydei frowned back at him. “That means it’s at least safe enough to walk around up there.”

“You’re just presuming that,” Phainon hissed. “If they’ve raided us twice it probably means they’re starving. It could be a wasteland up there!”

“We can’t stay down here in this bunker forever,” Mydei spat. “Or is that what you want?”

Phainon faltered. His grip on Mydei’s sleeve loosened.

Mydei shrugged him off. He went to pick up the rifle. He stood still in the dark for a few moments.

“One of us needs to protect the bunker,” Mydei said with his back turned, his voice quieter. “I’ll go, you stay here. I’ll leave you with the baseball bat, in case the raiders return.”

“Why have I got to stay?” Phainon scowled. He was starting to see spots in his vision, his breathing becoming chaste.

“I’m better equipped for this than you.”

“How!?” Phainon yelled. “That’s just bullshit and you know it!”

Mydei spun around to face him. “Stop arguing with me Phainon!”

“Mydeimos,” Phainon growled, balling his fists. He felt tears pricking his eyes as his world began to spin. “There is no way in hell that I’m letting you go up there.”

Mydei heard the upset in his voice and his own anger faltered. He sighed, turning back to the other. “Phainon-”

“-All this time and all I have been trying to do is protect you!” Phainon exclaimed. “You’re really gonna go out there and throw away that promise we had to stay together? If I lose you I have nothing left! Nothing! I’d rather kill myself than let you go up there alone!”

Mydei froze in place, his eyes going wide.

Phainon stared gravely in Mydei’s direction. “Mydei, I’m telling you to wait a little longer. If there’s people out there, then maybe we’ll get a radio message sooner than later…Mark my words, if you take one more step towards that door…I will hurt you.”

A beat of silence ticked between them, before Mydei let out a huff, rolling his eyes.

“You’d hurt me to keep me safe?” Mydei scoffed. “You’ve gone crazy.”

Phainon picked up the baseball bat. He tested it in his hands, a loud slapping sound as it hit his own palm. His expression remained dark, fixated on the other across the space.

Mydei’s eyes widened. That was enough to tell Mydei that the other meant every word.                 

They remained like that, locked in a standoff, until Mydei sighed, dropping the rifle to the floor.

“Fine. Have it your way.”

Phainon watched Mydei discard his jacket, his shirt, and his rifle. The blond man threw himself against their pile of blankets, burying himself underneath it. In that small space, that was his only way to have some time on his own.

Phainon didn’t feel guilty in any way.

All he felt was relief.

He gently put the baseball bat down and made his way over.

Mydei’s body was tight and rigid beneath the blankets. Phainon patted a hand over the blankets, feeling how Mydei went taunt underneath.

Mydei said nothing when Phainon slid beneath the sheets beside him.

He said nothing when Phainon clung to him, arms sliding around him to lock him in place against his chest.

“I’m just so scared to lose you,” Phainon whispered into the dark. “You’re…everything to me.”

Mydei didn’t respond. Phainon wondered if he’d even heard it.

After a while, Mydei finally sighed.

“I know, idiot,” he mumbled. Mydei raised his hands, settling them over Phainon’s, which were wrapped around his torso. “…I feel it too.”

Phainon’s heart melted. He pressed his forehead against the back of Mydei’s neck, as if he could embrace him any tighter. He breathed in Mydei’s calming scent.

“Then stay here. With me. Don’t go out…Please.”

Phainon pressed a light kiss to the back of Mydei’s neck.

Mydei’s breath hitched. Did that kiss make his resolve waver, or was he really that taken aback?

Phainon waited for him to respond, breathing in his scent all the while.

Suddenly, Mydei whipped himself around. He pinned Phainon beneath him on the sheets.

The next moment, Mydei leaned down and kissed him.

It was so much for Phainon to take in. By the time he went to kiss back, Mydei was already pulling away, his face flushed pink to the tips of his ears and panting gently.

“A few more days,” Mydei said eventually, through chaste breaths. “Then we will have to rethink our plans. Got it?”

Phainon felt tears in his eyes. He reached up, caressing Mydei’s cheek. Why did Mydei look so sad, his once stoic golden eyes had shattered, now bursting with emotion.

He looked so beautiful.

“…Mydei.” Phainon’s breath hitched. He caught his arms around Mydei’s neck, pulling him back down. “Yes…Okay…”

They didn’t need to say anything else.

All Phainon wanted was to have Mydei’s taste on his lips, to feel him everywhere. He kissed him like he was already starved, like they already had no hope left.

By the way Mydei kissed him back, hungry and desperate, he felt the same.

 

In the middle of the night, Mydei slipped his clothes on quietly. His rug sack was still packed from earlier before their fight. He slung the rifle over his shoulders. He’d already done the difficult part of untangling himself from Phainon’s embrace without waking him.

Now, he planned to leave quickly.

However, he noticed the diary on the desk. He picked it up, brushing his hands over the leather cover. He flicked through the pages of his mother’s and Phainon’s writings, all the notes and musings he’d made. He brushed against some of the words, the sentiments. Then, he turned to a new page. He hesitated, before picking up a pen.

 

Day 30: Phainon.

 I’m taking the key to the padlock with me so you can’t follow. If I have not returned by the time you wake, keep the baseball bat on your person. Remain vigilant, stay safe and await my return.

I’m sorry.

 

I love you.

 

Mydei left a space on the page, and found himself placing a gentle kiss there.

Then, he focused himself on the mission at hand.

Halfway up the ladder, he spared a final glance to Phainon’s sleeping figure. His heart squeezed tightly.

Then, he made off into the outside world.

 

When Phainon woke, he hummed to himself. His hand stretched across the pillows, reaching for the man he loved.

His eyes shot awake when he realised the pillow beside him was cold.

The first thing he noticed was the missing rifle, the missing bag pack, the deafening silence.

Then, he found the entry in the diary.

He screamed, wrestling with the padlock, but it was indeed tightly shut.

He wrestled with it, cursing Mydei’s name, until his hands were red and sore.

After however long, he fell to the floor and wept.

 

Day 31: Mydei left whilst I was asleep. He’s locked me inside and gone off with the key.

Bastard. I could kill him. Who does he think he is going off on his own!?

Did he kiss me so I’d have something else to think about whilst he is gone? Was that his promise to come back?

It better be.

I’ve been fighting with the lock all day. Seems all I can do is wait for him to come back.

I can’t help but flinch at every little sound from the outside, hoping each one is him.

Miss Gorgo, I’m sorry I couldn’t stop him.

 

Day 32: Mydei’s not back yet.

I continue to try to pry open the door. I can’t wedge it open no matter how hard I try. I think Mydei must have put something heavy on top of the trapdoor to stop me getting out.

Mydei, how could you?           

 

Day 33: Mydei’s still not back. The wait is torture. He promised to return and I trust him to the end. He will come back. He will…

 

Day 34: Mydei’s been gone for three days. I can’t hear anything. His scent is getting lighter in here.

I keep crying his name. I’m terrified.

 

Day 35: When are you coming back?!

Mydei…

Please…come back!

 

Phainon woke that night to a clatter above his head. He must have somehow dozed off at some point, burying his nose in the remainder of Mydei’s scent which stuck to the sheets. It sounded like someone was trying to get inside the bunker.

Phainon was instantly on his feet. He grabbed the baseball bat, before setting it down again. It sounded like someone was fiddling with the lock on the outside.

Could it be…?

His prayers were answered a moment later.

The instant he saw a flick of strawberry blond hair, Phainon was screaming and running forward.

He caught Mydei as he fell down the ladder into the bunker and collapsed in his arms.

“Mydei! Mydei? Can you hear me? Mydei!” Phainon fussed over him, checking his pulse, his temperature, trembling as he tried to process what was happening.

Mydei clung to him weakly, heaving as if he was about to vomit. Somehow, he managed to curl his arms around Phainon’s neck and pull himself close.

“Phai…non…” He groaned, his voice hoarse.

Mydei was in a poor condition. His clothes were tattered and covered in blood. His hair had almost turned brown from dust and dirt. He was trembling and had a high fever. Worst of all was the large stab wound on his chest, which was bleeding out onto Phainon’s hands.

“Oh titans. Shit,” Phainon mumbled to himself. He swept his fingers through Mydei’s hair, pulling his bangs from his eyes. “Hang on Mydei. I can fix this. Just hang on, please!”

Phainon rushed to lay Mydei down on the blankets and then grabbed their med kit. He pulled off Mydei’s shirt, uncaring for the cans of food that fell from Mydei’s pockets and rolled across the floor.

Phainon inspected the wound. The wound was large on his chest, however it didn’t seem too deep. Phainon could only hope he hadn’t suffered any internal bleeding from it. It seemed like Mydei had tried to treat it himself at some point. Phainon could see burn marks and stitches from where he’d tried to close the wound himself, only the stitches had come out at some point, and the wound was open and bleeding again. Around the edges of the wound, Mydei’s skin had started to go yellow and black. It was ugly, a bad sign that it was getting infected.

Mydei’s whole body heaved, as if it was difficult for him even to breathe. His eyes remained unfocused.

He was finally back, and Phainon couldn’t even feel relief.

“Shit…”

Phainon shook so much he could barely open the med kit.

Mydei arched his head back and closed his eyes, hissing in pain as Phainon tried to disinfect his wound with antibiotic ointment and cotton wool.

“I’m sorry, I’m sorry,” Phainon apologised profusely.

He knew he needed more antibiotics, the bottle was already empty.

The wound was still bleeding, and Phainon knew that he couldn’t leave it open.

There was a stitching kit inside the first aid box, and Phainon got to work quickly, disinfecting the needle with the last of the antibiotic ointment. He tried to dry Mydei’s wound as much as he could, before preparing the needle and stitches.

He squeezed Mydei’s hand briefly.

“Mydei, I’m going to stitch your wound closed. It might hurt a little, okay?”

Mydei groaned to him in response. His fingers dusted across Phainon’s own.

Phainon shuddered down his tears. He had to focus. For Mydei.

 

After stitching up the wound, Phainon did his best to clean it again with the little supplies he had. He then grabbed a roll of bandages, and began dressing it. He wove the bandages around Mydei’s chest, securing them tightly.

“H-how’s that?” Phainon stuttered once he was done. “Is that better, Mydei? How do you feel?”

He brushed his thumb over Mydei’s cheeks. Mydei’s face was incredibly flushed and hot. Phainon decided that he should wet a towel and place it on Mydei’s forehead.

“I’m sorry…Phai,” Mydei whispered. Mydei was looking up to him now, but it was clearly a strain to even do that. Phainon could see the pain swimming in his unfocused eyes.

Phainon grabbed his hands. “N-no! Don’t be sorry!” He leaned down. “You can be sorry when you’re better.” Phainon nuzzled their noses together. “You’re lucky I have bigger priorities right now. I won’t be so forgiving when you can stand on two feet.”

Phainon was biting back his tears and failing, especially when Mydei nuzzled him back.

“You were…right…” Mydei breathed. “It’s horrible…out there. I only managed to get…And I saw…” Mydei shuddered, recalling something.

“Ssh,” Phainon whispered, whisking a hand through his hair. He placed a kiss to the tip of Mydei’s nose. “Just focus on getting better, kay?”

Mydei hummed in response, leaning in to Phainon’s touch. He reached out for Phainon’s hand, and Phainon took it, giving it a reassuring squeeze.

“Missed you…” Mydei mouthed, closing his eyes.

Phainon leaned down, joining their mouths together. He kissed Mydei as gently as he could, his tears staining Mydei’s cheeks.

“I know…I know…”

 

Day 36: I woke to a clatter. Mydei returned. He’s covered in blood and can barely walk. He has a nasty stab wound on his chest. I used the med kit to try and treat it as best as I could. I’ll check it again in the morning.

I could scream at him for leaving me, for getting so injured. But at the same time, I’m just so relieved to see him.

I have him in my lap right now, stroking his hair as he sleeps.

I’ll pray to any god that he makes it through the night.

 

Day 39: I’ve barely slept for days. I can’t take my eyes off Mydei. I think his wound is already infected. I was too late. He keeps vomiting the food I feed to him, flitting in and out of consciousness. We’ve used up most of the pills and painkillers we had. It’s bad. I’m scared he’s not going to make it.

He needs to go to a hospital but I don’t know if that’s possible right now. I don’t know without scouting out the area. If it’s not, then we need more medical supplies, and more food.

I made him promise not to go out of the bunker on his own again and he agreed.

However, I’ve already made my decision. I won’t tell him because I know he won’t let me.

I will go out tonight under nightfall whilst he’s sleeping.

He’ll hate me for it, but it might be the only way I can save him.

 

Phainon inspected the rifle. There were a few bullets left in there. He would leave it here with Mydei. He would take the baseball bat instead. He also had a dagger strapped to the inside of his thigh if he had no other option.

Phainon put on his jacket, and flung the rucksack over his back. He went over to where Mydei’s jacket hung on the back of their deckchair. From the pocket, he pulled the key to the padlock.

His heart beat fast in his chest as he turned the key over in his hands, but he’d already committed to this decision.

“Phai…?”

Phainon heard the voice and winced. Mydei was awake, trying to sit up from the pile of blankets. Phainon had dosed him up on the last of their tablets and painkillers. For now, Mydei’s fever was stable. Still, the wound in his side was delicate, and the infection had spread. It was painful for him just to try and sit himself up.

Phainon went over to him, pushing him back down.

“Go back to sleep, my love.” Phainon whispered, kissing his forehead. But Mydei had already seen what he was wearing, understood what he was doing.

Mydei grabbed his wrists.

“No,” he said with all the bite he could muster. “Don’t do this. You don’t know what it’s like up there.”

Phainon couldn’t bear to look at the desperate plea in Mydei’s eyes. So instead, he wrapped him into an embrace.

“This might be the only way to save you,” Phainon whispered. “To save you, I would go to the end of the world again and again. We are lucky I only have to take one trip this time.”

Mydei shook his head, clinging to him with all his strength.

“If you don’t come back then I-”

“I will come back. And when I do, you better be here waiting for me.” Phainon took Mydei by the chin, making their eyes meet. “Promise me, Mydeimos. You’ll be here waiting for me.”

Mydei’s eyes were welling with tears. Had Phainon not already washed his emotions dry and focused himself on the mission at hand, seeing Mydei cry like that might have ruined him.

“No…please,” Mydei mumbled.

“Promise me.”

“Phainon!”

Phainon brought him in for one last kiss. Mydei tried to weave his fingers through Phainon’s clothes so that he couldn’t pull away.

But he was so weak that when Phainon pulled back, his grip simply melted away.

 “I’m leaving you the rifle,” Phainon said. “I’ll be back as soon as I can. Please…stay safe.”

Phainon made his way to the ladder, unlocking the padlock with the key. All the while, Mydei was calling after him.

Phainon couldn’t help but look back at the man he loved a final time.

His last image of Mydei barely looked like the man he’d fallen in love with. The man he’d made silly jokes with in the bar, trying to pretend his friends hadn’t set them up on a date. This Mydei was weak, frail and desperate. He’d been ruined by the end of the world.

It was that sight that made Phainon completely certain that to leave him behind and risk everything to save his life, was the right choice.

 

Day 40: I went out of the bunker in search of a way to save Mydei’s life.

I can’t describe the things I’m seeing up here well. The sky is still red, and the air feels heavy with rust and blood. Burned cars, destroyed buildings and half-eaten bodies stretch as far as my legs can carry me. Monsters lurk in the shadows. The evidence of the catastrophe that’s happened is everywhere. It’s all too much to take in, but I can’t let my guard down for a moment.

I’ve plundered a few shops but found no supplies just yet. That means someone else has already beaten me to it. I passed by the city hospital only to find it raised to the ground. No one was left alive there.

I’ve had to tackle several monsters already. Three tried to pursue me here, where I’m currently trying to catch my breath. I’m pretty sure there is a shopping mall in this direction. Since the hospital is gone, I think that’s my best shot.

I’ve already been gone from Mydei for almost a day. I can’t afford to be much longer.

 

Day 41: I reached an abandoned mall. Somehow, I managed to plunder some canned food. There was an abandoned pharmacy in the mall. It still had some products on the shelves. Unfortunately I wasn’t the only one to find it.

I had a standoff with another group of people over the medical supplies. There wasn’t enough for us to share, and I need medicine for Mydei. When they wouldn’t back down I ended up attacking them with my bat. After that I grabbed everything I could carry and ran.

Mydei, I’m coming. I promise. Please be waiting for me.

 

He was covered in sweat, dried blood, and haze from the sky. He hadn’t slept in three days. His legs ached, a migraine pounded through his head.

And still, Phainon ran.

When Phainon unlocked the trapdoor of the bunker and opened it up, the first thing he did was cry out.

“Mydei! I’m back! Mydei!?”

There came no response from inside, setting all Phainon’s worst fears into motion.

He quickly scrambled inside, falling down the ladder as he did so.

It took a moment for his eyesight to adjust to the darkness.

When they did, he could finally take the breath he’d been holding for days.

Mydei was there. Right beneath the ladder. Perhaps he’d been waiting there ever since Phainon had left.

He was in a bad state, struggling to breathe and wracked by sweat.

But the moment Phainon was at his side, Mydei was throwing his arms around him and burying his face against Phainon’s neck.

“Phainon you…bastard!”

Phainon could hear the shudder in his voice, could feel Mydei’s tears against his neck, the way he trembled in a way he could no longer control.

Phainon hugged him tight, letting himself enjoy their reunion for just a moment.

He hadn’t let himself feel anything save unshakeable determination for three days.

Finally, all his emotion was coming back to him.

“I missed you too,” Phainon cried, tearing up. “Titans, I was so scared that I was too late. Fuck Mydei, I love you so much.”

Mydei tried to kiss him, but Phainon stopped him. “Not right now. Let me look at your wound first.”

He picked Mydei up, and carried him back to their bed of blankets. Mydei didn’t argue, letting Phainon unwrap the bandages around his stomach. Phainon winced at the sight of the wound. It looked even worse.

As Phainon treated the wound with the supplies he’d gathered, Mydei kept his hands in Phainon’s hair, rubbing at his scalp gently.

Once he was done with that, Phainon dosed Mydei up on tablets and painkillers, before rifling through his bag pack, pulling out all the cans of food he’d been able to find.

“I’ve got some food for you as well,” Phainon said, splitting open a can of tinned fruit. He put some food onto a spoon, holding it up to Mydei’s mouth. “Eat.”

Mydei didn’t even look at the food. He blinked at Phainon.

“When are you going to kiss me?” Mydei asked simply and quietly.

“Eat this, then I’ll kiss you.”

“How much?” Mydei pouted.

“You gotta eat at least half of this can,” Phainon said.

“No,” Mydei pouted. “How much are you going to kiss me?”

Phainon blinked in surprise at the question. “…Is kissing all you’re concerned about?”

“Yes,” came the immediate answer.

Phainon could almost laugh at how Mydei pouted, pissed off that the lover who’d left him alone in a bunker at the end of the world for three days to try and find supplies that could save his life, didn’t come back and smother him in kisses straight away.

Perhaps Mydei was just delirious, or perhaps, his concern for Phainon’s life had melted away every barrier he had.

Phainon found himself smiling fondly. It was probably the first time he had smiled in over a week.

“Then eat this, and I’ll kiss you all night long, kay?”

Mydei seemed happy with that answer. Phainon helped him eat, lifting the spoon to his lips. Mydei didn’t even grumble about being babied. He ate everything without a fuss.

Then, he took the spoon from Phainon’s hand and threw it aside. He still had cheeks full of food; hadn’t even swallowed it yet.

Phainon had barely put down the half-eaten can of food when Mydei grabbed him by the string of his hoodie, and pulled him in for a kiss.

Phainon could taste the tinned peaches on Mydei’s tongue. He pried Mydei’s mouth open with his tongue, and let the other slip food into his own mouth.

Phainon swallowed the peaches Mydei had saved for him, savouring the taste of Mydei’s drool in his mouth. Then, without pulling apart, he negotiated for Mydei to lie back. Phainon went onto all fours above him. In that position, he could kiss him optimally; could kiss him like it was just the two of them at the end of the world.

Mydei hummed pleasantly against him, melting into every kiss. His arms went slack, and he was happy to let Phainon take control.

And Phainon was sure he could ravage him right then and there.

They made out noisily, their messy make out session filling the small quiet space of the bunker with disgusting sounds and noises.

When they pulled back, a long string of saliva continued to connect their lips.

Phainon didn’t wipe it away. Instead, he began trailing his lips down Mydei’s neck, licking marks everywhere he could manage.

“Fuck, Mydei,” Phainon whined. “Missed you…so much.”

Mydei groaned above him, fingers weakly gripping at the pillow beneath his head. Phainon kept going down, kissing all down his chest. “Love you, I love you.” Phainon swirled his kisses down to Mydei’s abdomen, savouring every part of him, bathing in every little movement of his body, every tiny moan.  Phainon looked at the bandaged wound on Mydei’s chest, kissing around it. “I would…kill myself… if I lost you.”

When Phainon looked back up Mydei’s body, he was greeted with the beautiful sight of Mydei splayed out across the blankets. A deep blush had settled in his cheeks. His long hair messily swept this way and this. His golden eyes shone lowly in the dark. His body heaved, breathless and needy.

His condition was bad, but his desire for Phainon was greater.

Mydei reached out to him. Phainon let a weak hand pull him back up, until their lips were pressing again.

“You’re insane,” Mydei mumbled against his lips.

“We’re just two lonely souls at the end of the world,” Phainon whispered back, tearing up again. “Is it really that bad to be a little crazy for the one thing I have left to cherish?”

Mydei smiled against his mouth. They shared a gentle, more intimate kiss.

“I guess not,” Mydei murmured, wiping the tears from Phainon’s eyes. “So long as you kiss me more.”

“Hmm,” Phainon hummed. “I don’t mind doing that.”

 

Day 42: Me and Mydei stayed beneath the blankets all day. His condition doesn’t seem any worse than last night. I guess it’s still too early to see if the new medication is working. I’ll keep dosing him up often.

We didn’t talk that much about the things we saw out in the world. I just want to hold him tight, and he just wants to kiss me and tell me off for leaving him. That’s more than okay though.

 

Day 44: The medication is working. Mydei’s getting a little stronger by the hour. His wound is still a concern. All I can do is keep cleaning it, keep changing the bandages regularly and hope for a miracle.

Mydei told me not to worry too much. He doesn’t seem concerned. It’s reassuring to see him more like himself either way.

 

Day 45: We spent all night mapping out each other’s bodies with our lips. I want to make love to him. I want to be the one to set his body on fire. When his wound is better, I might try going further with him. I wonder if he’ll let me lead?

 

Day 46: A broadcast came through on the radio! They are sending people out to search for survivors! They urged anyone in the area to tune into the frequency and await instruction over the next few days. They’ll let us know when we can go outside. Me and Mydei almost cried with relief. It really is a miracle! Once we get out, they’ll be able to treat his wound.

I think we might be okay.

I can’t believe all of this is actually about to come to an end...

 

The instruction came through on the 48th day:

‘A rescue team is in your area. Any survivors, please come onto the streets and await for a scout. They will escort you to a safe area.’

 

Phainon smiled and took Mydei’s hand. Mydei smiled back at him. He was still weak, and needed support to walk, but strong enough to stand on his own.

They opened the padlock, and together, ascended up the ladder.

Hand in hand, they walked amongst the remains of their world.

They were greeted with a silent world. All screams had long dissipated and all fires had flickered out. Rubble littered the streets, the roads, everything that once stood had now decayed and brought to its knees by destruction.

However, the sky above their heads was a mix of red, orange and yellow, like the dawning of a new day, a new life.

After walking for a while, Phainon saw something on the road ahead.

“Look, there!”

He pointed to the thing in the distance. It seemed like some kind of truck.

The two of them waved and shouted trying to get the driver’s attention.

They beamed when the truck began approaching them.

As it got closer, Phainon heard Mydei’s breath hitch.

“Is it…?”

Phainon squinted in Mydei’s direction. Sat on top of the truck, a familiar head of long purple hair. Beside her, another lady they both knew too well, with a head of gorgeous gold.

Phainon smiled so wide at the sight. He couldn’t believe it.

“Castorice! Aglaea!” He waved, ugly tears rolling down his face. “Over here!”

He could hear Castorice shouting their names. She was already jumping from the truck, and running towards them.

Phainon felt something squeeze his hand. He looked to his right, where Mydei smiled at him. His long hair blew gently in the breeze, the colours of the sky highlighting the undying gold of his eyes.

“We made it,” Mydei said simply.

He was beautiful before the end of the world, he was beautiful through the end of the world.

And now, at the new dawn, he was still the most beautiful thing Phainon had ever seen.

Phainon’s breath hitched, before he smiled back.

“We did,” he said, tucking some hair behind Mydei’s ear.

 

Not even the end of the world could tear them apart.

And that’s how it would remain.
